messages:
Alex P: Quick heads-up — Enterprise customer 'Mapboxx' wants to purchase via GCP Marketplace but needs a 12mo committed rate with a special rate card and monthly billing to match their procurement cadence. Can we apply a committed discount through the marketplace and still align invoices with their PO? :thinking_face:
Sophie (SE): TL;DR technical POC looks good. From infra side nothing blocks marketplace usage. Main constraint is commercial/billing. GCP Marketplace typically invoices customer directly, so they won't get a separate Redwood invoice if it goes purely through the marketplace. :eyes:
Taylor (DealDesk): Do we know the ask size and target ARR? Need numbers to evaluate commit/case. Also: can the commit live as a private offer? If so, we can negotiate a private pricing plan and include a commit discount.
Alex P: Asking for a 12mo commit, ~$300k ARR (consumption-style). Procurement insists on receiving monthly invoices to reconcile with internal costing. They also want our standard SLA & data residency addenda on contract.
Jamal - Billing: Marketplace mechanics: GCP charges customer and pays us out (minus marketplace fee ~20% and payout delay). We can't issue a separate monthly invoice to the customer for the portion sold via GCP Marketplace unless we do a dual-contract approach (direct contract + marketplace buy). That adds complexity.
Maria S - Procurement: Clarify: customer will only accept a single vendor invoice on their books, ideally Redwood. If marketplace forces GCP invoice, CFO will flag. Any hybrid flow we propose must be signed off by our Finance.
Chris L - Finance: If we accept a private offer through GCP, revenue recognition and cash flow change (payout schedule, chargebacks). Margin hit from marketplace fee ~20% needs to be baked into pricing. Also need to confirm if commit can be grossed up (i.e., higher list price on marketplace to preserve net to us). That requires Marketplace Partner team sign-off.
Sophie (SE): For POC/buying path options: 1) Direct contract + meter-based billing (we invoice monthly) — requires customer to buy off-contract, not via marketplace. 2) GCP Private Offer — customer purchases via marketplace, we create a private pricing offer with committed SKU. 3) Hybrid: Customer takes baseline via marketplace for procurement ease, we give post-sale credits or rebate under direct SOW for the committed portion. Each has pros/cons.
Taylor (DealDesk): Can we do option 2 with custom terms? If they require our MSA, GCP often prevents full custom T&Cs in standard marketplace flow. Private offers sometimes allow limited contractual attachments (SOW) but GCP legal will still govern billing. We need Legal to confirm.
LegalBot: Marketplace private offers can include an attachment (SOW) but customer acceptance and billing are still subject to GCP's Marketplace Terms. If the customer requires our MSA with specific indemnities or data residency clauses, marketplace alone may not suffice. Workaround: execute Redwood MSA + GCP private offer for procurement convenience; but must be explicit about which terms govern billing vs service. This is a redline-able scenario.
Marketplace Partner Bot: We can create a Private Pricing Offer (PPO) with a committed SKU. To preserve net dollars to Redwood, we often increase list price to cover Marketplace fee, then show discount in the private offer. Partner team needs the final net target and effective dates.
Alex P: Example sketch (not final):
```
private_offer: true
sku: RED-INF-COMMIT-12
list_price_per_unit: $0.20/token
commit_term: 12 months
commit_value: $360,000
marketplace_fee: ~20%
net_to_redwood: ~$288,000
```
Taylor (DealDesk): If we gross up list to hit net target, procurement will see a higher list price — may trigger additional approvals. Also need to check if GCP allows showing both list and private discount amounts on the offer.
Jamal - Billing: Operational notes: payouts from GCP are subject to their payout schedule; we might have a delay of 30–60 days. For customer invoicing (monthly PO reconciliation) the cleanest is direct invoicing. If customer insists on single vendor invoice, we should propose direct contract and then register the spend in GCP marketplace as a 'consumption record' for billing convenience — requires partner engineering.
Maria S - Procurement: Customer also asked about tax handling and VAT. Marketplace handles tax calculation in many regions; direct invoicing we'd need to collect VAT ourselves. Which is simpler for them? Probably Marketplace, but they want Redwood on the invoice.
Chris L - Finance: Two asks for us: 1) target net revenue after marketplace fee, 2) agree to payout timing and forecast impact. Without those, Finance can't sign off on the commit.
Alex P: Real ask from customer: "We need a 12m committed price, billed monthly, with our PO on each monthly invoice, and Redwood contractual terms." Seems like a hybrid is necessary. Can we approve: private offer through GCP for procurement convenience + Redwood monthly invoice/credit for the committed discount?
Taylor (DealDesk): That triggers an exceptions approval (commit-exception) — I'll start the Deal Desk request. Need: final numbers (net target), whether legal accepts hybrid doc flow, and SE confirmation POC is done.
Sophie (SE): POC ✅. Customer signed acceptance tests yesterday.
LegalBot: I'll draft language for hybrid flow and flag clauses about SLA, indemnity, and data residency. Need to know which clauses customer insists on.
Marketplace Partner Bot: Partner team can spin up a PPO once Deal Desk confirms target gross price and effective dates. Estimated lead time: 3–5 business days to get private offer ready.
Alex P: Action items: 
- Taylor (DealDesk) owner for exceptions request (timeline: EOD today to file).
- Chris L (Finance) to confirm net target and payout tolerances by tomorrow.
- LegalBot to prepare hybrid redline template.
- Marketplace Partner Bot to standby for PPO creation.
- Jamal - Billing to outline monthly crediting flow if we do hybrid.
Maria S - Procurement: I'll push customer to accept a private offer if that speeds procurement. If they still insist on Redwood invoice only, we'll need to run direct-contract path.
Taylor (DealDesk): Filing request now. Please drop final numbers in this thread as soon as you have them. :white_check_mark:
Alex P: Thanks all — will follow up with the customer's exact PO wording and the clauses they require.
